name: King's Pawn Game
summary: Classical symmetrical opening fighting immediately for central space and quick piece development.

name: Italian Game
summary: White aims the light-squared bishop at f7 while preparing rapid castling and a central d4 or c3 break.

name: Giuoco Piano
summary: Quiet Italian development leading to rich positional maneuvering or sharp central pawn breaks.

name: Two Knights Defense
summary: Active counterattack against e4 inviting tactical complications like Ng5 or quiet d3 play.

name: Ruy Lopez (Spanish Opening)
summary: One of chess's deepest openings, putting lasting pressure on Black's knight defending e5.

name: Ruy Lopez: Berlin Defense
summary: Ultra-solid counterattack on e4 favored by elite players for resilient endgame structures.

name: Scotch Game
summary: Direct central clash that opens lines early and avoids long Ruy Lopez maneuvering.

name: Petrov's Defense
summary: Symmetrical counterattack on White's e4 pawn aiming for clean, balanced piece activity.

name: Four Knights Game
summary: Classical, principled development bringing all four knights into play before committing pawns.

name: Vienna Game
summary: Flexible opening preparing f4 or Bc4 while keeping the f-pawn unblocked.

name: King's Gambit
summary: Romantic pawn sacrifice seeking rapid f-file pressure, central dominance, and tactical attacks.

name: Sicilian Defense
summary: Asymmetrical fighting defense contesting d4 from the flank and creating dynamic imbalances.

name: Sicilian Defense: Najdorf Variation
summary: Sharp, ambitious Sicilian fighting for b5 expansion while controlling the key b5 square.

name: Sicilian Defense: Dragon Variation
summary: Black fianchettoes the dark-squared bishop on g7 to aim a powerful diagonal down the board.

name: French Defense
summary: Resilient counterattacking structure challenging White's e4 pawn with solid pawn chains.

name: Caro-Kann Defense
summary: Solid defense supporting d5 without locking in the light-squared c8 bishop.

name: Scandinavian Defense
summary: Immediate central challenge forcing White to resolve the e4-d5 pawn tension on move two.

name: Pirc Defense
summary: Hypermodern setup letting White build a broad center before counterattacking it with c5 or e5.

name: Alekhine's Defense
summary: Provocative hypermodern defense tempting White's pawns forward to become future targets.

name: Queen's Gambit
summary: Classical wing-pawn offer to deflect Black's d5 pawn and seize superior central control.

name: Queen's Gambit Declined
summary: Time-tested central defense keeping a strong pawn foothold on d5.

name: Slav Defense
summary: Compact support for d5 that keeps Black's light-squared bishop free to develop outside the chain.

name: London System
summary: Reliable, low-theory system developing the dark-squared bishop early before solidifying with e3.

name: King's Indian Defense
summary: Dynamic hypermodern defense aiming for rapid castling and a fierce kingside or central counterattack.

name: Nimzo-Indian Defense
summary: Strategic pin on the c3 knight fighting for control of the e4 square and structural flexibility.

name: Grünfeld Defense
summary: Counterattacking system inviting White to build a large center and then undermining it with pieces.

name: Catalan Opening
summary: Positional squeeze combining Queen's Gambit central pressure with a powerful g2 fianchetto.

name: English Opening
summary: Flexible flank opening controlling d5 and often transposing into reversed Sicilian structures.

name: Réti Opening
summary: Hypermodern knight-first approach attacking Black's center from the wings.

name: Dutch Defense
summary: Ambitious asymmetrical reply to 1.d4 immediately claiming control over the e4 square.
